paragraphs: Rubbish is harder to model than product. A crumpled box has no symmetry and no clean edges, and it is exactly what a street scene, a bin or a table after a meal needs to stop looking staged.
The model is extremely light at 2,836 polygons and 2,815 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits street and interior scene dressing, waste and environmental visualisation, film and television sets, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

Aluminium is worth crushing because it is worth recycling, and a flattened can takes a fraction of the space. It is also one of the most photographed pieces of litter in the world, which is a different argument entirely.
The model is very light at 6,336 polygons and 6,090 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 4 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits recycling and environmental visualisation, street and interior scene dressing, film and television sets, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

Decanting spirits is theatre rather than chemistry. Nothing improves in the glass, but the vessel says something about the occasion, and the weight of the stopper is a significant part of what the buyer is paying for.
The model is very light at 13,172 polygons and 13,178 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with stopper. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits tableware and hospitality visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, bar and interior scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A lipstick in pencil form is a precision argument. It draws a line rather than covering a surface, which is why it is sold to people who outline before they fill, and why the cap and the sharpener matter as much as the colour.
The model is extremely light at 1,496 polygons and 1,518 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits cosmetics and product visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, dressing table scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Coiled rope is stored the way it is because a bundle that is not laid properly will knot itself the moment it is thrown. Every trade that uses rope has a preferred coil, and each one is a solution to that.
The model is very light at 8,056 polygons and 8,072 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in dirty condition. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits industrial and marine visualisation, workshop and site scenes, film and television set dressing, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The tower on a bar is the visible end of a system that runs to a cellar. It is chilled along its whole length, because beer that warms in the last metre arrives foaming, and the brass is doing conductivity as well as decoration.
The model is very light at 5,636 polygons and 5,848 vertices, built at subdivision level with non-overlapping UVs, in brass. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits bar and hospitality visualisation, equipment marketing, interior scenes, e-commerce imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2021.

The robot emoji is a face with antennae, and that is enough. It has come to mark anything automated, from a helpful assistant to an accusation that a person is not one, which is a considerable range for one pictogram.
The model is extremely light at 2,586 polygons and 2,612 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits motion graphics and social content, technology advertising, presentation and infographic work, animation, game interface assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The skull emoji stopped meaning death almost entirely. It now marks something so funny the sender is claiming to have died, which is one of the fastest and most complete semantic shifts any symbol has undergone.
The model is extremely light at 3,774 polygons and 3,779 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits motion graphics and social content, advertising and marketing visuals, animation, game interface assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
The woozy face carries a specific and difficult meaning: not quite drunk, not quite ill, somewhere between amused and defeated. It is used constantly for exactly the situations no other emoji covers.
The model is extremely light at 3,800 polygons and 3,788 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits motion graphics and social content, advertising and marketing visuals, animation, game interface assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

An empty decanter is a different photograph from a full one. The facets have nothing to refract, so the object reads as sculpture rather than as a container, which is how it spends most of its life on a shelf anyway.
The model is very light at 11,636 polygons and 11,640 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, empty with a faceted stopper. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $19 it suits tableware and interior visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, bar and dining scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The rubber stopper and aluminium crimp are the whole design. A vial is entered with a needle and resealed by the rubber closing behind it, which is what allows multiple doses to be drawn from one container.
The model is extremely light at 3,032 polygons and 3,040 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.
At $19 it suits medical and pharmaceutical visualisation, packaging and label mockups, clinical and laboratory scenes, e-commerce imagery, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

A broadcast stick microphone is designed to be seen. The triangular flag on it is advertising, the shape is chosen so a logo reads from any angle, and the audio requirements are almost secondary to that.
The model is light at 18,836 polygons and 10,153 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $19 it suits broadcast and media visualisation, sports and news scenes, equipment marketing, character accessories, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The skipping rope is the cheapest serious piece of training equipment there is, and boxers have known it for a century. The handles carry bearings so the rope turns freely, which is the only part with any engineering in it.
The model is very light at 5,832 polygons and 5,862 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 10 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits fitness and sports visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, gym scenes, character accessories, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.
A dropper is a dosing device disguised as a lid. The bulb draws a repeatable volume, the pipette places it precisely, and the whole format exists for liquids where a splash would be the wrong amount.
The model is very light at 9,144 polygons and 4,664 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, prepared as a mockup. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $19 it suits packaging and label mockups, cosmetics and pharmaceutical visualisation, e-commerce imagery, advertising, bathroom scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
